stem: A trivalent lanthanide ion has a spin-only magnetic moment of $\sqrt{35}$ BM. How many unpaired $4f$ electrons does it have?

verdicts.working: Using μ = √[n(n + 2)] BM: n(n + 2) = 35, so n = 5.

working:
$\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}$

Independent check: Using μ = √[n(n + 2)] BM: n(n + 2) = 35, so n = 5.
solution:
For a spin-only magnetic moment, $\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}$ BM, where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons.
$$\sqrt{n(n+2)}=\sqrt{35}\;\Rightarrow\;n(n+2)=35\;\Rightarrow\;n=5$$
Thus, it has $5$ unpaired $4f$ electrons.
